**Harmoni Murni Catering Sdn. Bhd. (SYN‑001199)**  
- **Status & Structure:** Active private limited company incorporated on 24 Oct 2004 in Selangor. Share capital RM 2.5 million. Formerly known as *Kirana Industries Sdn. Bhd.* (name change 26 Sep 2024).  
- **Industry & Business:** Food & Beverage – wholesale distribution of frozen food to restaurants.  
- **Ownership & Management:**  
  - Directors: Managing Director (Director 1, appointed 30 Jun 2013), Independent Director (Director 2, appointed 16 Jan 2007), Executive Director (Director 3, appointed 31 May 2007).  
  - Shareholders: Director 1 (individual) – 89.6 %; Director 3 (individual) – 10.4 %.  
- **Financial Highlights (FY‑end March):**  

| Year | Revenue (RM) | Gross Profit Margin | Operating Profit | Net Profit (RM) | Total Assets (RM) | Total Liabilities (RM) | Leverage (Debt/Equity) |
|------|--------------|---------------------|------------------|-----------------|-------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| 2022 | 9.22 M | 54.1 % | –RM 0.80 M | –RM 0.95 M | 6.25 M | 3.99 M | 1.77 |
| 2023 | 10.19 M | 53.8 % | –RM 0.17 M | –RM 0.34 M | 6.91 M | 4.99 M | 2.60 |
| 2024 | 12.29 M | 58.5 % | RM 0.85 M | RM 0.49 M | 8.33 M | 6.07 M | 2.68 |

- **Trend:** Revenue grew ~33 % over three years, moving from a loss‑making position in 2022‑23 to a profit of RM 491 k in FY 2024. Gross margins improved, and operating profit turned positive (8.9 % of revenue).  
- **Liquidity:** Quick ratio consistently above 1.6 (2022 = 1.63, 2023 = 1.61, 2024 = 1.73); cash‑to‑revenue around 3–7 %.  
- **Cash Flow:** Operating cash flow swung from –RM 1.07 M (2022) to a modest +RM 13 k (2023) and a strong +RM 0.60 M (2024). Free cash flow remains slightly negative in 2024 (–RM 28 k).  
- **Capital Structure:** Debt levels rose, with leverage climbing to ~2.7 × equity in 2024. Interest coverage turned positive in 2024 (ICR ≈ 4.2), after being negative in prior years.  
- **Litigation:** No recorded court cases.  

**Overall Assessment:** Harmoni Murni Catering has transitioned from a loss‑making, highly leveraged distributor to a modestly profitable, cash‑generating business in FY 2024. Liquidity is healthy, but the company remains debt‑heavy; continued improvement in operating efficiency and debt reduction will be key to sustaining profitability.
